title: mögen, gern, lieber, am liebsten
definition: These words express likes and preferences. Mögen is a conjugated verb meaning 'to like'; gern describes doing something gladly; lieber compares preferences; am liebsten expresses the strongest preference.

rules.title: mögen — to like
rules.explanation: Mögen is a verb and changes according to the subject.

rules.title: gern — like doing something
rules.explanation: Place gern after the conjugated verb to say that you enjoy doing an activity.

rules.title: lieber — prefer / rather
rules.explanation: Use lieber to compare activities or things you prefer.

examples.german: Ich trinke lieber Tee als Kaffee.
Sie liest lieber als sie fernsieht.
examples.english: She prefers reading to watching TV.

rules.title: am liebsten — like best
rules.explanation: Use am liebsten to express your favourite activity or strongest preference.

examples.english: I like listening to music best.
Pizza is what I like eating best.

examples.german: Wir reisen am liebsten mit dem Zug.
examples.english: We like travelling by train best.

rules.title: Compare the patterns
rules.explanation: Mögen is used with a noun; gern/lieber/am liebsten commonly describe how much you like an action.

examples.english: Most of all, I like drinking water.

common_mistakes.explanation: In a simple main clause, the conjugated verb is in position two.

common_mistakes.wrong: Ich mag gern Fußball spielen (when intending a simple preference).
common_mistakes.explanation: For liking an activity, a simple A1 pattern is verb + gern.

mastery_goal: You can talk about your likes, preferred activities, and favourite things using the four common patterns.
